questions.stem: A sphere has radius 6 cm. What is its volume in terms of pi?
A ball has diameter 22 cm. What is its volume to the nearest cm cubed?
questions.explanation: Radius = 11 cm. V = (4/3) pi (11)^3 = (4/3) pi (1331) = 5324 pi / 3 = 1774.67 pi = 5575.28... which rounds to 5575 cm cubed. Using diameter instead of radius is a common error.

questions.stem: A sphere has volume 972 pi cm cubed. What is its radius?
questions.explanation: (4/3) pi r^3 = 972 pi. So (4/3) r^3 = 972, giving r^3 = 972 x (3/4) = 729. Therefore r = cube root of 729 = 9 cm.

questions.stem: A hemispherical bowl has internal radius 10 cm. How many litres of soup can it hold? (1 litre = 1000 cm cubed). Give your answer to 2 decimal places.
questions.explanation: Hemisphere volume = (2/3) pi r^3 = (2/3) pi (1000) = 2000 pi / 3 = 2094.395 cm cubed. In litres: 2094.395 / 1000 = 2.09 litres.

questions.stem: If the radius of a sphere is doubled, by what factor does its volume increase?
questions.explanation: Volume depends on r^3. If the radius doubles, volume increases by 2^3 = 8 times.
